sentences.text: Staphylococcus capitis is a coagulase-negative staphylococcus described as a commensal bacterium of human skin that must also be considered an opportunistic pathogen.
The species is divided into two subspecies, Staphylococcus capitis subsp. ureolyticus and Staphylococcus capitis subsp. capitis.
A comparative genomic study called it primarily a human skin commensal now emergent as an opportunistic pathogen of the bloodstream, prosthetic joints and neonatal intensive care units.
A virulent clone designated NRCS-A has been reported to be responsible for outbreaks of neonatal sepsis, primarily in Europe.
In 42 extremely preterm neonates, S. capitis made up 13 percent of coagulase-negative staphylococci on skin or mucous membranes, and septicemia isolates belonged to the NRCS-A clone.
